Mr. Vishesh Wadhwa, learned counsel appearing on advance notice, accepts notice on behalf of the respondent No. 2.
7.

Learned counsel for the applicant/petitioner has placed reliance on the decision of the Co-ordinate Bench in Pradeep Santolia and Others vs. State and Another, 2018 SCC OnLine Del 13428.
8.

entities.text: Pradeep Santolia and Others vs. State and Another, 2018 SCC OnLine Del 13428
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Additional Standing Counsel on behalf of the State submits that the present application is a mala fide because the respondent No. 2/Complainant has made various Complaints against the conduct of the petitioner and the petitioner in order to save himself, has preferred the present application.

He also submits that the present Application is also not maintainable as the present petition seeking quashing of the FIR No. 152/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 has been allowed vide Judgment dated 31.05.2023.

9. Learned Additional Standing Counsel on behalf of the State further submits that the judgment in Pradeep Santolia, (supra) which has been relied upon by the counsel for the petitioner is not applicable to the fact of the present case as in that said case, while arriving at a settlement, the parties had agreed to the visitation rights/custody rights of the child which had been endorsed by way of the said Judgment.
10.
It is submitted that the present Application is mala fide and is liable to be dismissed.
11. Submissions heard.

12. The record shows that on the basis of the Settlement Agreement dated 04.05.2022, the FIR No.
152/2022 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/09/2024 at 21:10:49 Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered at Police Station Dwarka South, Delhi has been quashed vide Judgment dated 31.05.2023.

As per the Clause No. 5 of the Settlement Agreement dated 04.05.2022, the parties had agreed that the custody of the minor daughter shall remain with the mother/respondent No. 2-Complainant and that the petitioner/father shall have no visitation rights qua the child.

13. The petitioner now, almost after two years, has preferred the present Application seeking visitation rights qua the minor child, the custody Order in respect of the child is inherently interim and is subject to modification in view of the change in circumstances in future.

14. Moreover, the Settlement Agreement dated 04.05.2022 inter se the parties does not determine the rights of the minor child and, therefore, the present Application is misplaced since the petitioner is seeking visitation rights, for which he is at liberty to move an appropriate Application before the Competent Court, in accordance with law.
